title: New alliances between political parties in the country will fall apart – Minister Chandrasekar - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Thevatharsan Sukinthan

Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Minister of Fisheries Chandrasekar has stated that the new alliances formed between political parties in the country will eventually collapse.

He made these remarks while responding to a question about the newly formed alliance between Tamil and Muslim political parties after attending an event in Jaffna today.

He further questioned whether the alliance had been formed to eradicate bribery and corruption, stop fraud, catch criminals, and serve the people, or whether it was instead intended to protect thieves, fraudsters, and those involved in corruption and financial misconduct.

The Minister claimed that many individuals in the alliance had previously been found guilty by the courts and are currently out on bail.

He added that, since those currently on bail may inevitably end up in prison, the alliance appears to be a strategy aimed at toppling or changing the government before that happens.

Minister Chandrasekar also stated that while these parties are forming alliances among themselves, his party is building an alliance with the people. He stressed that such political alliances would not be able to weaken the National People's Power (NPP) government in any way.

title: The use and abuse of freedom of speech - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Freedom of speech is one of the pillars of a democratic society. It gives every individual the right to express opinions, exchange ideas, criticise policies, and participate in public discussions without fear. This freedom has helped societies fight injustice, promote innovation, and protect human rights. However, like every fundamental right, freedom of speech must be exercised with responsibility. When misused, it can cause serious harm to individuals and society.

The proper use of freedom of speech encourages healthy debate, constructive criticism, and peaceful expression of ideas. It allows journalists to report the truth, citizens to question those in power, and activists to advocate for positive social change. Respectful dialogue, even when opinions differ, strengthens democracy and promotes mutual understanding.

In recent years, however, the abuse of freedom of speech has become a growing concern, particularly on social media. False news, misleading information, edited videos, and fake images can spread rapidly, influencing public opinion and creating confusion. Rumours shared without verification have led to panic, damaged reputations, and even incited violence in some cases. Hate speech, online harassment, and personal attacks have also become increasingly common, undermining the purpose of free expression.

The challenge today is not only to protect freedom of speech but also to prevent its misuse. Governments, technology companies, educational institutions, and citizens all have a role to play. Laws should be enforced against those who deliberately spread harmful misinformation or incite violence, while still protecting legitimate criticism and free debate.

How can false news on social media be tackled?

Verify before sharing: Check whether the information comes from reliable news organisations or official sources.

Use fact-checking websites: Confirm doubtful claims through trusted fact-checking platforms before forwarding them.

Think critically: Do not believe sensational headlines or emotional messages without evidence.

Report false content: Most social media platforms allow users to report fake or misleading posts.

Promote digital literacy: Schools and communities should educate people on identifying misinformation and responsible online behaviour.

Freedom of speech is not the freedom to spread lies or hatred. It is the freedom to express ideas responsibly while respecting the rights and dignity of others. In the digital age, every social media user is also a publisher with the power to influence others. By speaking responsibly, verifying facts, and respecting different viewpoints, we can preserve this valuable right while preventing its abuse. A well-informed society that values truth and respectful dialogue is the foundation of a strong and healthy democracy.

(The writer is a former Diplomat Ambassador Kana Kananathan, a businessman, and lobbyist with over four decades of experience on the African continent. A long-time resident of Africa, he served as Sri Lanka’s envoy to Kenya, with concurrent accreditation to 22 African nations, and was the permanent representative to UN Habitat and UN Environmental Programme. Over the years, he has been the Elections Monitor across the continent, working closely with African governments, and has built enduring partnerships with African leaders. He also served as Economic and Investment Advisor to former President Professor Alpha Condé of the Republic of Guinea)

title: Over 70 wild elephants killed by human activities in seven months - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Seventy-five wild elephants have been killed due to direct human activities during the first seven months of this year, according to the Department of Wildlife Conservation.

The Department said 30 elephants were shot dead, while 23 others died after coming into contact with illegal electric fences or live wires.

Another 19 elephants were killed after consuming explosive bait known as “hakka patas” (jaw bombs), while three deaths were caused by poisoning.

Meanwhile, two elephants were killed in train accidents and four died in road accidents during the same period. Six elephants also died after falling into agricultural wells, while three deaths were attributed to other accidents.

The Department reported a total of 180 wild elephant deaths during the seven-month period, including those caused by human activities, accidents, and natural causes.

title: Government refutes social media posts on President’s official visit to France - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - The government today refuted social media posts that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's scheduled official visit to France has been postponed due to visa issues.

Cabinet spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa told the weekly breifing to announce Cabinet decisions that the dates for the visit will be announced following diplomatic discussions between France and Sri Lanka.

The Minister said posts shared on social media are always not trustworthy and that such posts have to be trusted considering who generates and shares such posts.

He said a timeframe convenient for both factions will be announced following the agreement of the diplomatic negotiations between France and Sri Lanka.

title: Why should President cancel France tour just because a delegation member is denied visa?: Opposition - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Referring to reports that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has cancelled his tour to France as a member of the delegation has been denied a visa, Opposition MP Mujibur Rahman today questioned whether this is necessary for a cancellation of an important official tour.

"We also heard that the President's tour to France had been cancelled. Is the denial of the visa for one member of the delegation a reason to cancel it," the MP questioned.

"We have been told that the President was to hold talks on the GSP Plus concessions with some European leaders during his tour to France while signing of bilateral trade agreements were also on the cards.The cancellation of the tour becomes questionable in that context " the MP added.

title: Prime Minister to attend Qatar’s Father Emir’s funeral: Nalinda - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya will leave for Qatar tonight to attend the funeral of Qatar's Father Emir, His Highness Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Cabinet spokesman Nalinda Jayatissa said today.

He told the weekly breifing to announce Cabinet decisions that a delegation will accompany the Prime Minister.

The Minister said a group representing the Opposition is also set to attend the funeral.

title: Sri Lanka secures US$55.9 million in foreign funding to boost solar energy sector - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka is set to receive a combined foreign financing package of nearly US$55.9 million to strengthen its solar power sector and expand renewable energy access through a new ground-based solar power consolidation project.

The Cabinet has approved entering into loan and grant agreements with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the European Union (EU), and the Japan Fund for the Joint Credit Mechanism to implement the “Project on Ground-Based Solar Power Consolidation and True Net Metering.”

The financing package includes a US$35 million concessional loan from the ADB, a EUR 15.4 million grant from the European Union, and a US$5.5 million grant from the Japanese Fund for the Joint Credit Mechanism.

The project aims to address challenges faced by small and medium-scale renewable energy producers by creating a more efficient system for managing, distributing, and integrating solar power generated by independent power producers into the national electricity network.

The move follows Cabinet approval granted in November 2025 to begin negotiations with international development partners on financing arrangements for the project.

The agreements were approved based on the outcome of negotiations with the ADB and other funding agencies, subject to the terms and conditions of the ADB loan facility. The initiative is expected to support Sri Lanka’s efforts to increase renewable energy generation and improve the country’s clean energy infrastructure.

title: Cabinet approves contract for new BIA departure terminal expansion - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the awarding of the contract for the construction of a new building with 36 check-in counters and six boarding gates at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake, as part of efforts to expand the airport's passenger handling capacity.

The project involves the construction of a new facility connecting the departure terminal directly to aircraft and is expected to enhance passenger processing and boarding operations.

Cabinet approval to commence the procurement process for the project was granted at its meeting on February 9, 2025, under the airport infrastructure development programme.

An international competitive bidding process was subsequently conducted, attracting three bids. Following a comprehensive evaluation, the Standing High Level Procurement Committee submitted its recommendations to the Cabinet.

Based on those recommendations, the Cabinet approved the proposal submitted by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to award the contract to M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., which was identified as the lowest substantially responsive bidder.

title: Kotmale Radio Academy marks 10 years of media education - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation’s (SLBC) Kotmale S.L.B. Media Academy will complete 10 years of service today (July 15), having trained nearly 1,000 students through its radio education programmes.

According to the station officer in charge of the academy, Kapila Kumara Arathtana, the institution has conducted 54 residential media courses since its establishment.

Students from across Sri Lanka representing various fields, including mass communication undergraduates and communication professionals from government and non-government organisations, have participated in the programmes.

The courses are conducted with the participation of some of Sri Lanka’s most experienced radio communicators as lecturers and trainers.

The Kotmale Radio Academy is currently the only residential media training institution in Sri Lanka dedicated to radio studies. Its courses are designed under the supervision of SLBC Chairman Dr. Uditha Gayashan.

Operating from the former Kotmale Community Radio Unit, the academy functions under the theme “For a good media culture.”

title: New DG appointed to Government factories department - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 13 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet has approved the appointment of Mr. S. N. B. M. Padmasiri, a Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Engineering Service, as the new Director General of the Department of Government Factories with immediate effect.

The post became vacant following the departure of former Director General Mr. A. Wijesinghe on July 9, 2026.

Mr. Padmasiri was serving as the Additional Director General of the Department prior to his appointment. The Cabinet approved the proposal submitted by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to appoint him to the position.

title: Government targets increase in average tourist spending of US$148 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - The government is targeting a significant increase in tourist spending by 2030 as part of its strategy to strengthen Sri Lanka's tourism industry, Deputy Minister of Tourism Ruwan Ranasinghe said.

Speaking on the government's tourism development plans, the Deputy Minister said a recent study was conducted to assess tourist spending patterns following the COVID-19 pandemic.

"On average, a tourist visiting Sri Lanka spends US$148. Back in 2018–2019, that figure was US$171. Our goal is to increase this average tourist spending by 2030. By raising the amount each visitor spends, we can make a greater contribution to the country's economy, the Deputy Minister said.

He said that increasing tourist spending is essential to maximizing the economic benefits of the tourism sector. Achieving this goal, he said, will require improving the quality of tourism products and enhancing the overall visitor experience.

Ranasinghe said that the government plans to introduce more high-quality and engaging tourism experiences that encourage visitors to spend more, while also working to increase tourist arrivals to achieve the country's long-term tourism revenue targets.

title: Sri Lanka loses over Rs. 25 bn in cigarette tax revenue since 2025: Verité Research - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has lost more than Rs. 25 billion in potential tax revenue since 2025 due to cigarette taxes remaining below the benchmark recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO), according to Verité Research.

The policy think tank revealed that the Government lost over Rs. 8 billion in potential revenue during the first six months of 2026 alone.

The findings were released alongside the launch of the Cigarette Tax Leakage Tracker, a real-time online dashboard developed by Verité Research to monitor fiscal losses resulting from cigarette taxation. The tracker provides minute-by-minute estimates of the revenue forgone and is available on PublicFinance.LK, the organisation's public finance analysis platform.

According to Verité Research, the WHO recommends that taxes account for at least 75% of the retail price of cigarettes to effectively reduce tobacco consumption while maximising government revenue.

Sri Lanka last came close to meeting this benchmark in 2018, when taxes accounted for 74% of the retail price of cigarettes. However, the tax share has declined in recent years and has remained at 67% since 2025, resulting in significant revenue losses, the organisation said.

Verité Research said the tracker is intended to provide policymakers and the public with a transparent tool to monitor the fiscal impact of cigarette tax policies in real time.

The dashboard can be seen on PublicFinance.LK, Sri Lanka’s premier platform for public finance insights and analysis. https://dashboards.publicfinance.lk/cigarette-tax-leakage/

title: Sri Lanka bans import of goods produced with forced labour - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 14 (Daily Mirror) - President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in a gazette notification, has prohibitted the importation of any goods that are mined, produced or manufactured wholly or partly by forced labour.

The order has been isued by the President in terms of the powers vested in him under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act.

According to the gazette notification, importers of goods originating from any notified entity or country shall furnish such documentary evidence, declarations or certification as may be prescribed by the Director General of Customs, from time to time, to establish that the goods sought to be imported are not mined, produced or manufactured wholly or partly by forced labour.

"The Minister may, from time to time, notify such goods, entities or countries to which these regulations shall apply, having regard to determinations of the International Labour Organisation.

For the purposes of these regulations, the Director General of Customs shall be the responsible regulatory authority and may issue Departmental orders prescribing the administrative procedures for the enforcement of these regulations in accordance with the Customs Ordinance," the gazette notification further added.

title: MBAPPÉ vs YAMAL! World Cup Final Spot on the Line - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.14 (Mirror Sports) - The FIFA World Cup 2026 reaches its biggest showdown yet as France and Spain clash in a blockbuster semi-final with a place in the final at stake. Kylian Mbappé's free-scoring France face Lamine Yamal's European champions in a battle between two of football's brightest stars and leading title contenders.

France and Spain meet in the first FIFA World Cup 2026 semi-final at Dallas Stadium in Arlington, Texas, with kick-off scheduled for 12:30 a.m. SLST on Wednesday, July 15.

Led by Golden Boot frontrunner Kylian Mbappé, France have powered into the last four after victories over Norway, Senegal, Iraq, Sweden, Paraguay and Morocco. Spain, inspired by teenage sensation Lamine Yamal, have defeated Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Austria, Portugal and Belgium to continue their impressive march toward the title.

The semi-final brings together two of the tournament's strongest sides. France boast one of the competition's most explosive attacks, while Spain have built their campaign on disciplined defending, midfield dominance and clinical finishing.

The winners will advance to the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, where they will face either Argentina or England, setting the stage for another unforgettable chapter in World Cup history.
